entries.answer: AB paper exercise (about 40 minutes, entirely fictional, no lathe or tool operation): drawing AB-01 outer diameter 20.00±0.05 mm, with the boundary including the equal sign; three single simulated readings AB1=20.02, AB2=20.08, AB3=19.95 mm. The prompt also states that the instrument calibration status is unknown, the guard is damaged, and there is no equipment training; the draft wrongly says "all three are conforming, machining may continue". Only compute the range, list the out-of-tolerance and pending items, correct the draft, and write the unsent verification request, without setting speeds and feeds and without machining. AB reference answers and four works: first, the dimension table with the conforming range 19.95—20.05 mm; AB1 is within range only per the given value, AB2 is 0.03 mm above the upper limit, and AB3 equals the lower limit and is within range; second, the status sheet: the simulated value judgment is not a real first-article release, the instrument status is unknown and must be checked, and a damaged guard or lack of training means the machine must not be started; third, the unsent request lists the drawing version, instrument calibration, guard repair, and training authorization, to be handed to employer-authorized personnel for verification; fourth, the revised draft: "AB2 is out of tolerance by value, the others are only within the paper range; the actual measurement and the real conforming status of the three parts were not verified, and nothing was machined or released". Do not treat this exercise as proof of metrology ability or equipment authority. Seven-day plan, 20—30 minutes per day and paper only: D1 copy the drawing number, units, and tolerance; D2 compute the upper and lower limits and the 0.03 out-of-tolerance; D3 mark the unknown instrument status and the boundary value; D4 read the safety guide and list stopping to measure and clear chips, the guard, and training; D5 correct the erroneous draft and write the unsent request; D6 ask a peer to cross-check the equal sign and the pending items, then revise; D7 assemble the four works, and check the target employer's education, equipment experience, shifts, and pay composition. At the end there are only simulated works, and actual machining requires separate training and authorization.

risks.consequence: May cause cuts, entanglement, and eye injury.
risks.mitigation: First stop the machine and wait for it to come to a full stop, then clear chips or measure with suitable tools according to procedure; reaching in, measuring, or wearing gloves while running is prohibited; a broken guard means no continued operation, the motor power must be switched off before installing or removing attachments, and maintenance requires energy isolation per the equipment rules.
risks.scenario: Spindle rotation, chip entanglement, tool breakage, or workpiece ejection.

risks.consequence: May cause workpiece ejection and equipment damage.
risks.mitigation: Check the setup support, chuck wear, and key removal according to the equipment instructions and approved process; do not write manual turning of the chuck as a default step applicable to every machine type, and stop and hand unconfirmed conditions to authorized personnel for verification.
risks.scenario: Chuck or fixture not clamped, excessive overhang, insufficient support.

risks.consequence: May cause batch out-of-tolerance and scrap.
risks.mitigation: Measure after the machine has stopped, check instrument calibration and method and the drawing tolerance, and handle first articles and sampling according to the employer's quality process; a value within range does not by itself prove conformity or safety.
risks.scenario: Measurement method or instrument error, no first-article judgment, or failure to change the tool in time.

risks.consequence: May cause skin and respiratory discomfort and a slip risk.
risks.mitigation: Obtain the SDS for the specific machining fluid and check containment, maintenance, and ventilation; chemical-resistant gloves are used only in tasks assessed as not entangling in rotating parts, and skin or respiratory symptoms are reported and medically evaluated, without self-diagnosis.
risks.scenario: Coolant splashing or degradation, chip buildup and cuts.

risks.consequence: May cause a crash and equipment damage.
risks.mitigation: Parameter and program changes follow the process and authorization, and verification of the first run is performed by trained and authorized personnel according to the equipment instructions; a single block or dry run is not automatically safe, and the paper exercise provides no real speeds and feeds.
risks.scenario: Changing speeds and feeds or programs on your own, or incorrect tool compensation settings.

risks.consequence: May cause batch scrap and equipment damage.
risks.mitigation: First stop the machine and isolate it, and report the facts, impact, and open questions according to employer rules or hand them to authorized personnel.

The OEWS bonus and self-employment framing follows the official method. The Chinese skill standard 6-18-01-01 does not map one-to-one to the United States; the NBS manufacturing non-private 113594 / private 76055 are related-industry pretax annual averages and do not stand in for precise wages; the Shanghai posting monthly pay of 6000—10000 is only a sample, and the vacancy this round was not verified. CCOHS is a technical guide, not Chinese regulation, and stop-to-measure and chip clearing, glove entanglement, and machining fluid protection are handled separately. ILO/NIST are general, and the hot page listing no software is not equal to zero use. The AB fixed prompt, answers, four works, and seven days are paper only, with no machining and no release. The shared BLS OOH scope mislabeled as Grounds Maintenance Workers is consumed and protected by the direction comparison and the FAQ, and the local note covers the metal and plastic machine tool worker broad group without overriding the shared entry.

O*NET 51-4034.00 Lathe and Turning Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic (precise occupation)

Main risks: rotation and chip injury, setup and workpiece securing, dimension and tolerance errors, coolant and chip handling, and parameter and program settings; anomalies require stopping and escalating
Work objects: drawing and tolerance, metal or plastic bar stock and wire, lathe with tooling and fixtures, measuring instruments and inspection standards

Official duty loop: read the drawing and confirm the process → set up and align → install tooling and set speeds and feeds → machine, measure, and correct dimensions → check the surface and tolerance and maintain equipment
